title: Completion of a stable nonarchimedean field is stable
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. Suppose $k$ is stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]. Let $H=\widehat k$ be its metric completion [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion], equivalently equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences for $|x-y|$, with termwise field operations and absolute value $|[(a_n)]|=\lim_n|a_n|$. Then $H$ is stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]: every finite field extension $L/H$, with its minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_{L/H}$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], has an $H$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ satisfying $$s_{L/H}\left(\sum_i h_i b_i\right)=\max_i |h_i|s_{L/H}(b_i)\qquad(h_i\in H).$$ No completeness of $k$ and no separability of $L/H$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/3, printed p.158 (scan PDF p.166), completion criterion; proof supplied by the agent because the local archival document is absent.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion], $H$ is a complete normed field containing $k$ isometrically and densely. The nonarchimedean inequality on $H$ follows by taking limits of that inequality on approximating sequences in $k$; nontriviality follows from its restriction to $k$. By [lem-trf-complete-stability-separable-criterion] it suffices to prove the orthogonal-basis assertion for every finite separable extension $F/H$. Fix one. By [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension] its spectral norm is a multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value extending that of $H$. By [lem-per-finite-normed-space-complete], $F$ is complete. Apply [lem-trf-dense-subfield-separable-descent] to $k\subseteq H\subseteq F$. It supplies a finite separable subextension $E/k$ inside $F$ which is dense in $F$, with $HE=F$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/3, ascent, first paragraph; Proposition 3.6.2/2 and Krasner descent

proof.text: Write $s=s_{E/k}$. By [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] this is a definite ultrametric $k$-algebra norm. Stability of $k$, unfolded using [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field], gives a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ with $s(\sum a_i e_i)=\max_i|a_i|d_i$, where $d_i=s(e_i)>0$. Put $c=\min_i d_i>0$ and $C=\max_i d_i$. Then $c\max_i|a_i|\le s(\sum a_ie_i)\le C\max_i|a_i|$. Thus [lem-trf-weak-spectral-completion-product] applies to $E/k$: its normed completion $A=\widehat{(E,s)}$ is an $n$-dimensional $H$-algebra, with extended norm $N$, and an isometric $H$-algebra decomposition $A\simeq\prod_{j=1}^r L_j$ with $N=\max_j s_{L_j/H}$. This uses the spectral norm on $E$, which need not be its absolute value inherited from $F$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/3, ascent, spectral completion and its norm-direct-sum decomposition

proof.text: The images $b_i$ of $e_i$ in $A$ form an orthogonal $H$-basis. Indeed, for $h_i\in H$ choose $a_{i,t}\in k$ tending to $h_i$. Scalar multiplication and the extended norm in step 2 give $$N\left(\sum_i h_i b_i\right)=\lim_t s\left(\sum_i a_{i,t}e_i\right)=\max_i|h_i|d_i.$$ For spanning, represent $z\in A$ by an $s$-Cauchy sequence $z_t=\sum_i a_{i,t}e_i$. The estimate $|a_{i,t}-a_{i,u}|d_i\le s(z_t-z_u)$ makes every coordinate Cauchy in $k$. Its limit $h_i\in H$ satisfies $N(z_t-\sum_i h_ib_i)\to0$, whence $z=\sum_i h_i b_i$. The displayed formula implies linear independence because every $d_i>0$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/3, ascent, completion preserves cartesian spaces (2.4.3/8), explicit finite-coordinate argument

proof.text: The inclusion $E\hookrightarrow F$ is contractive for $s$. For nonzero $z\in E$, its monic minimal relation $z^q+\sum_{i=1}^q a_i z^{q-i}=0$ gives $$|z|_F^q\le\max_i|a_i||z|_F^{q-i}.$$ If $|z|_F>s(z)=\max_i|a_i|^{1/i}$ every term on the right is smaller than the left, a contradiction. Hence $|z|_F\le s(z)$, also for zero. For an $s$-Cauchy sequence $z_t$, define $q([z_t])=\lim_t z_t\in F$. Completeness of $F$ gives the limit and the bound proves independence of representatives. Limits of sums and products show $q:A\to F$ is a unital algebra map: Cauchy sequences are bounded and $|z_tw_t-zw|\le\max(|z_t||w_t-w|,|w||z_t-z|)\to0$. For $h=[a_t]\in H$, $q([a_tz_t])=h\,q([z_t])$, so $q$ is $H$-linear and fixes $E$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/3, ascent, identify the completion factor inducing the valuation of F; explicit comparison and extension

proof.text: Under $A\simeq\prod_jL_j$, the coordinate idempotents have images under $q$ in $\{0,1\}$, since $F$ is a field. They sum to $1$, and no two can map to $1$ since their product is zero. Thus exactly one, indexed by $j_0$, maps to $1$, and $q$ factors through a unital $H$-field embedding $\phi:L_{j_0}\hookrightarrow F$. Pull back the norm of $F$ along $\phi$. It and the spectral absolute value of $L_{j_0}$ both extend the norm of the complete nontrivially valued field $H$; [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension] supplies the latter, and [lem-sfb-algebraic-absolute-value-unique] identifies them. The image of $\phi$ is finite-dimensional over $H$, hence complete for its inherited norm by [lem-per-finite-normed-space-complete]. It is closed in $F$: a convergent sequence in the image is Cauchy, has a limit there by completeness, and uniqueness of metric limits identifies that limit. It contains the dense $E$, because $q$ fixes $E$, so it is all of $F$. Consequently $F$ is isometrically $H$-isomorphic to this factor.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/3, ascent, the factor inducing the valuation on E has completion F

proof.text: Embed $F$ into $A$ by $\phi^{-1}$ followed by insertion in the $j_0$th product coordinate and the inverse of the decomposition in step 2. This is an $H$-linear isometry, since the product norm of a tuple supported in one coordinate is precisely that coordinate's spectral norm. Its image is a linear subspace of the finite cartesian space of step 3. Apply [lem-trf-cartesian-subspace] to this image and pull its orthogonal basis back through the isometry. We obtain an $H$-basis of $F$ satisfying the exact maximum formula for $s_{F/H}$. Since $F/H$ was arbitrary finite separable and $H$ is complete, [lem-trf-complete-stability-separable-criterion] proves stability of $H$, including its inseparable finite extensions.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/3, end of ascent; subspace permanence (2.3.3/4) and Proposition 3.6.2/2
